rv.q: A stunning production with a talented young cast who skilfully tell this relevant and resonating story, allowing and encouraging the audience to question entrenched beliefs and consider new perspectives.
Engaging performances by a committed cast make this production a lively and fascinating coming-of-age story.
Choir Boy is a fantastically performed, written and directed coming-of-age piece of theatre.
The performances are 1st rate and we really didn't recognise Jarrett from his diametrically opposite turn in Juniper Blood.

Nancy Medina's production of Choir Boy remains a powerful exploration of how young men are encouraged to exert themselves in society, as long as they conform to a restrictive view of what constitutes masculinity.
Choir Boy has charm and wit, and there's plenty about which you can sing your praises, but it lacks a certain energy to capitalise on its warmth and tenderness.
